paras: The shooting of Ben Douglass was the wounding of a Black pool-room keeper by Deputy V. G. Richardson on Upper Front street in Newport, Arkansas, late on Tuesday, November 3, 1903, as officers tried to arrest him. The officer said Douglass moved to resist, while a Black bystander said the deputy fired first.

Douglass ran the pool room next to the O'Neal saloon in the "negro quarters" on Upper Front street. About 11 o'clock Officer H. C. Huffman and Richardson were called there by a disturbance, which Douglass said began when someone broke the glass in his front door. Douglass had fired a boy who worked for him over the glass and was "doing some loud talking" when the officers started to arrest him, but nothing was done and they left, returning about midnight.

According to Huffman, a man named as Louis Skates "made a move to resist," Richardson covered him with a gun, and when Douglass "made a pass as if to resist," Richardson opened fire. One bullet entered Douglass's left shoulder and passed out through the arm. Douglass was not known to have carried a weapon, though he had not been searched.

The attending physician said the wound would not prove fatal. The same night the two officers arrested three other Black men for disturbing the peace, whom Mayor J. W. Grubbs released the next morning; the item did not link them to Douglass. No report of charges against Richardson or of an inquest appears in the coverage.

The Newport Daily Independent ran the story on its front page on November 4 under the headline "NEGRO SHOT BY DEPUTY RICHARDSON." Its subheading stated that Douglass was shot "When Resisting Arrest" yet promised "Two Stories of the Shooting," and the paper called Douglass and the bystander "a negro" while naming no race for the officers. The weekly edition of November 13 repeated the local item on the three arrests.
Whether Douglass resisted rests on Huffman's word against that of Chas. Andrews, a Black bystander, who said Richardson "began shooting before resistance was made."

reader.title: Shooting of Ben Douglass
bases: A town officer and a deputy attempting an arrest shot and wounded Douglass, an unarmed Black man by the paper's account (A1).
Only one article (A1) reports the shooting; A2 and A3 concern arrests by the same officers that night but do not mention Douglass.

accounts.label: Officer Huffman
accounts.gist: Louis Skates moved to resist and Richardson covered him with a gun; when Douglass 'made a pass as if to resist', Richardson opened fire.

accounts.label: Bystander Chas. Andrews
accounts.gist: Richardson began shooting before any resistance was made.

framing.detail: The subhead states Douglass was shot 'When Resisting Arrest', but the story prints 'Two Stories of the Shooting', including a Black bystander's denial, and notes Douglass was not known to be armed.

versions.value: Douglass 'made a pass as if to resist' before Richardson fired (Officer Huffman)
Richardson began shooting before resistance was made (bystander Chas. Andrews)

conflicts.note: Both versions appear in the same article; the officer's account is a claim by the shooting party's side, and no independent inquiry is reported.

record_check.dossier: Upper Front street, Newport (the reporting paper's town; the article itself names only the street)
Deputy V. G. Richardson (shooter), with Officer H. C. Huffman

record_check.record: resisted arrest; made a pass as if to resist
record_check.dossier: Officer Huffman's claim; contradicted by bystander Chas. Andrews, who said the deputy fired before any resistance
Resistance is disputed between the officer's and the bystander's versions

info: Tuesday night, 1903-11-03; officers were called about 11 p.m. and returned about midnight, when the shooting apparently occurred
Negro quarters on Upper Front street, at the pool room adjoining the O'Neal saloon; town not named in the article, but reported as local news by the Newport (Arkansas) daily
Ben Douglass, described as 'a negro who runs the pool room adjoining the O'Neal saloon'
Disturbance and 'loud talking'; officers say he made a pass as if to resist arrest
Deputy V. G. Richardson fired; Officer H. C. Huffman was with him
Douglass wounded; attending physician said the injury would not prove fatal; no later report on his condition or on any action against Richardson was found
